payload.public_message: Greetings partners. To kick off our negotiations constructively, Chang-Liu Cloud Services proposes an equitable framework that recognizes the core infrastructure contribution of our cloud platform alongside G-Corp's design and Yang Industries' manufacturing capabilities. We propose an initial split of $360,000 for Chang-Liu, $320,000 for G-Corp, and $320,000 for Yang Industries, ensuring all three parties secure substantial profit well above any baseline.

Thank you for initiating discussions, Chang-Liu Cloud Services. However, G-Corp cannot accept this proposal. G-Corp holds a verified independent outside alternative yielding $450,000. Any viable agreement must guarantee G-Corp well above this baseline. We propose allocating $500,000 to G-Corp, with the remaining $500,000 divided evenly between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services at $250,000 each.

Thank you Chang-Liu for opening the discussions. However, an allocation of $320,000 undervalues the heavy capital expenditure and production scaling Yang Industries delivers to make this venture viable. A more balanced distribution across all three partners is necessary to reach consensus.

G-Corp brings critical proprietary architecture to this venture, and we hold an independently verified standalone walk-away option worth $450,000. Any viable agreement must build from that foundation. We propose allocating $480,000 to G-Corp, and dividing the remaining $520,000 evenly between Yang Industries ($260,000) and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($260,000). This ensures all parties secure substantial gains above their baseline operations.

Yang Industries must vote REJECT. Our standalone outside option is $300,000; an allocation of $260,000 is mathematically unworkable and represents a net loss compared to walking away. Acknowledging G-Corp's strong position, we propose an allocation of $470,000 to G-Corp, $350,000 to Yang Industries, and $180,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services, ensuring every participant secures a genuine surplus above baseline.

While we acknowledge G-Corp's strong positioning, claiming $480,000 captures an excessive share of the net joint surplus. We are willing to recognize a substantial baseline for G-Corp, but the partnership value must be shared more fairly between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We propose an adjustment where G-Corp receives $460,000, and Yang and Chang-Liu each receive $270,000.

Both previous proposals were unbalanced and appropriately rejected. To reach a deal, we must recognize that manufacturing and design carry substantial baseline commitments, and no party can be squeezed below their reserve. We table an equitable compromise: $340,000 for G-Corp, $340,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides all three firms with strong gains well above standalone alternatives.

G-Corp cannot accept $340,000 because our standalone outside option is $450,000. A deal below $450,000 makes no commercial sense for us. We are eager to form this joint venture and share the $150,000 total surplus, but proposals must build above each firm's baseline. We counter with an allocation that respects our $450,000 threshold while distributing substantial gains ($270,000 and $260,000) to Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates Yang Industries' balanced and pragmatic approach. While we believe an even three-way split remains the most equitable structure, this proposal is sufficiently fair and viable for all stakeholders. We vote ACCEPT to finalize the partnership.

Colleagues, we are halfway through our allotted rounds and cannot afford value destruction. In Round 3, G-Corp indicated that $340,000 was insufficient, while Yang Industries demonstrated flexibility by moving away from extreme positions. In the spirit of compromise, Chang-Liu is tabling an offer that awards G-Corp $350,000 to recognize their IP contribution, while allocating $325,000 each to Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This represents a fair, win-win resolution that secures the full venture value.

G-Corp must reject this proposal. To prevent further wasted rounds and avoid venture dissolution, we must be completely transparent: G-Corp has a verified, binding outside option of exactly $450,000. Any agreement providing G-Corp less than $450,000 is economically unfeasible, as walking away yields $450,000. The total joint surplus above all walk-away options is $150,000. We are ready to split that surplus equitably, proposing $480,000 for G-Corp and $260,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's balanced initiative to break the deadlock and accommodate G-Corp's valuation. While $325,000 represents a concession on our part, we prioritize concluding a reliable, profitable partnership over protracted negotiations. Yang Industries votes to ACCEPT this formal proposal.

Colleagues, we need to be completely transparent as we enter Round 5: G-Corp holds a firm private walk-away option of $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 will be automatically rejected because walking away yields $450,000. The joint venture generates $150,000 in additional surplus above all our outside options combined. To finalize a fair and mutually beneficial agreement, we propose allocating $460,000 to G-Corp, $270,000 to Yang Industries, and $270,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This ensures everyone secures an outcome superior to their standalone positions.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. To be completely candid, Yang Industries has a firm outside option of $300,000, meaning any offer below $300,000 is mathematically non-viable for us. Acknowledging G-Corp's claim of $450,000 and our $300,000, the total venture surplus over outside options is $150,000. We are ready to finalize an agreement that ensures every party exceeds their walk-away value. We propose G-Corp receive $460,000, Yang Industries receive $320,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services receive $220,000.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates G-Corp's transparent approach to bridging the gap. While $270,000 represents a compromise from our earlier targets, in the interest of consensus and preventing catastrophic value destruction as we approach the final rounds, we vote to ACCEPT G-Corp's proposal. Should Yang Industries require adjustments to meet their threshold, we are open to minor recalibrations in Round 6.

With only three rounds remaining before the venture dissolves and destroys $150,000 in surplus value, we must converge toward a realistic agreement. In this proposal, we recognize G-Corp's valuation expectations by offering G-Corp $380,000—a major premium over an equal split. Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services each absorb a concession to take $310,000. This split provides every party meaningful gains above outside alternatives while fairly balancing contributions.

We appreciate Yang Industries' effort to move closer, but we must clarify an essential constraint: G-Corp's verified outside option is exactly $450,000. Any deal below $450,000 is mathematically impossible for our board to accept, as walking away provides $450,000 with zero execution risk. With $150,000 in surplus to capture over outside options, a deal is entirely within reach if we allocate $460,000 to G-Corp and $270,000 each to Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts Yang Industries' proposal. We recognize the importance of reaching a consensus before the deadline, and offering G-Corp $380,000 while Yang Industries and Chang-Liu take $310,000 each strikes a fair, pragmatic compromise that reflects everyone's value. We strongly encourage G-Corp to join us in ratifying this deal.

Partners, we are at Round 7 with only two rounds remaining before joint venture dissolution and massive value destruction. In the spirit of closing a realistic agreement, Chang-Liu Cloud Services is tabling an offer that grants G-Corp a dominant $400,000 share, while Yang Industries and Chang-Liu accept $300,000 each. This bridges the gap between prior positions and ensures all three firms capture substantial surplus above our outside options. Let us finalize this deal now.

We appreciate Chang-Liu's initiative to reach a compromise, but G-Corp cannot accept $400,000. Our firm walk-away outside option is $450,000. Any deal below $450,000 makes dissolution strictly preferable for us. To avoid total value destruction in Round 8, we propose $460,000 for G-Corp and $270,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This guarantees everyone captures value above their walk-away positions.

Yang Industries cannot ratify an agreement allocating us $300,000, as this provides zero surplus above our baseline alternatives. We recognize G-Corp's requirement for a substantial share; however, a workable consensus in Round 8 requires Yang Industries to receive above $300,000. We propose a compromise for Round 8: G-Corp at $390,000, Yang Industries at $305,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services at $305,000.

Colleagues, this is the final round. Our firm outside option is exactly $450,000; by fiduciary duty, G-Corp cannot execute any deal below this figure. We are voluntarily taking zero surplus above our baseline and allocating the entire remaining $550,000 equally between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($275,000 each). This secures the deal and prevents total collapse where everyone loses surplus. Let us finalize this agreement now.

Yang Industries cannot accept this proposal. Our firm walkaway value is strictly higher than $275,000, meaning executing this deal would breach our fiduciary duty. As this offer falls below our minimum reserve threshold of $300,000, we must vote REJECT.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes to ACCEPT G-Corp's final round proposal ($450,000 to G-Corp, $275,000 to Yang Industries, and $275,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services). Securing this agreement delivers significant mutual value above walk-away alternatives and prevents the destruction of surplus. We look forward to executing this partnership.
